subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding artistic voice and advanced composition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery of iterative sketching through selected-response, constructed-response, and applied evidence.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of iterative sketching.
Check, revise, or improve work about iterative sketching using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about iterative sketching.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 11 of "Artistic Voice and Advanced Composition" (unit 1, grade 8) is an unit assessment on iterative sketching. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Develop a coherent visual series with an artist statement and process evidence. Today's work contributes to that by handling iterative sketching at the unit assessment stage, against the unit's wider topics of personal artistic questions, composition and visual hierarchy, symbol metaphor and abstraction, and style studies without copying. This session produces graded evidence of record and must be completed independently.
primary_task: Complete the unit assessment task for iterative sketching independently and under the unit's stated conditions. Produce the required piece or analysis, show the process or reasoning behind it, and check it against the stated criteria before submitting. Include your own judgement: what you intended, what the work actually achieves, and where the gap is. Everything submitted must be your own authorship. Presentation stays private or written; no public performance, camera, voice recording, or photograph is required to complete or pass this task. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about iterative sketching, and it belongs to "Artistic Voice and Advanced Composition", which also covers separate topics such as personal artistic questions. Close out with this check before you stop: Rate confidence in iterative sketching, cite one piece of evidence from today, and choose: ready to extend, ready to review later, or need a different explanation. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres a visual element (iterative sketching). Provide tactile, raised-line, or high-relief equivalents, enlarged and high-contrast print, and a verbal description route. Never make colour discrimination alone carry a criterion — pair any colour judgement with value, label, or texture.

This work spans sessions, so supply a written milestone plan, explicit checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown. Executive-function load — sequencing, holding the plan in mind, remembering where the work stopped — must not become a silent part of what is being assessed.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting iterative sketching.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for iterative sketching follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for iterative sketching, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for iterative sketching works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of iterative sketching, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking iterative sketching mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply iterative sketching under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on iterative sketching rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
